intro: Carpentry builds coordination, quality control and problem solving on the job site. The closest of the 25 careers below is Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic, with an 85% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $63,870, or 5% more than the $60,580 carpenters earn.
why_it_works: Reading plans, measuring twice and fitting parts that must line up are the core of layout, fabrication and rigging work. O*NET rates coordination at 3.25 out of 5 for carpenters, and quality control close behind at 3.12. Nearly all matches need no extra education. The new skills are mostly mechanical: maintaining equipment, running machines and troubleshooting when they fail.
tips: Show precision on your resume: tolerances you work to and the size of projects you framed or finished.
Consider power-line work, where installers earn $95,320, or 57% more than carpenters, after a paid apprenticeship.
Pick up welding or rigging certificates; both appear among your closest matches.

faq.q: What jobs can former carpenters do?
faq.a: The closest matches are layout workers (85%), Structural Metal Fabricators and Fitters (81%), and helpers for brick, stone and tile setters (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Riggers are close too at 76%, with a median of $62,640, which is 3% more than carpenters earn.

faq.q: Which careers for carpenters pay more?
faq.a: 10 of the 25 matches pay more than the $60,580 carpenter median. The largest gains are Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers at $95,320 (57% more), mining roof bolters at $78,540 (30% more) and Commercial Divers at $72,990 (20% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do carpenters need more education to switch trades?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than carpenters already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 60% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, so apprenticeships and certificates count more than degrees.

The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, operation and control, operations monitoring and troubleshooting. Complex problem solving already rates 3 out of 5 for carpenters in O*NET, so learning to run and repair machines is the main step.
